findings.claim: On device the main-looper Handler timer produced exactly one scheduling log and then never executed the callback: pendingCloseId stayed set (events kept logging ya tiene timer activo) and no timer-entry log ever appeared, so the close never ran. The schedule now uses serviceScope with kotlinx delay, the same coroutine machinery already used for WhatsApp processing in this service. Consequence: the close path no longer depends on the main-looper message queue for its critical section; if the coroutine also fails to run, the new timer-entry log will be absent while serviceScope-based WhatsApp logging still appears, isolating the failure to this feature rather than the timer mechanism.

handleWhatsAppEvent already runs work through serviceScope.launch on Dispatchers.Default

findings.location: app/src/main/java/com/example/projectacc/MyAccessibilityService.kt attempt retries and background thread access
findings.claim: The close now retries up to three times (500 ms, 1000 ms, 1500 ms) and runs node reads, parseOrder, and performAction on Dispatchers.Default instead of the event thread. AccessibilityNodeInfo property reads and performAction are binder calls safe to invoke from a background thread, but the node instances are now touched from a different thread than the event loop, so any future change that mutates nodes concurrently with an event pass could race. The fields shared across threads (pendingCloseId, lastClosedId) are annotated Volatile; retries stop at the first terminal outcome (closed or Cruz Verde rendered) so a closed popup is not clicked again.
proof_refs: attemptNonCvClose runs inside serviceScope.launch and recycles window roots before returning
lastClosedId and pendingCloseId declared with @Volatile and written once per terminal transition

findings.claim: hideKmOverlay is posted to the main looper via Handler.post after a successful background close instead of being called synchronously. WindowManager.removeViewImmediate must run on the main thread, so the post is required; the downside is that if the main looper is congested the km overlay hides late (cosmetic only, since later event passes also call hideKmOverlay). The popup click itself no longer depends on this post completing.
proof_refs: attemptNonCvClose posts hideKmOverlay through Handler(Looper.getMainLooper()).post after logging the click result
hideKmOverlay uses WindowManager.removeViewImmediate which requires the main thread
